semantic_dependency_limit: Graph edges sequence known planning and execution obligations. Prose contract prerequisites must be resolved in each package before implementation. Acyclicity alone is not proof that all architecture decisions are settled.

decisions.title: Baseline and scope
decisions.question: Which exact committed input and pending work belong to the next implementation generation?
decisions.required_output: A source/worktree custody ledger and explicit disposition of all 906 features, 611 targets, 174 contracts, 63 named implementations and the catalogue surface; Later/Profile labels retain scope.
decisions.acceptance: No missing or duplicate IDs; no dirty work overwritten; no historical done claim adopted without matching evidence.

decisions.title: Dependency and handoff semantics
decisions.question: Which bounded interfaces can be consumed before the owning phase is fully complete?
decisions.required_output: A named producer/consumer/ABI/error/ownership/proof contract per handoff, plus the distinction between development readiness and final phase promotion.
decisions.acceptance: Resolve process/credentials, file-backed memory/VFS, host-language/target-toolchain and browser/app-platform bootstrap cycles explicitly; all executable edges must be acyclic.

decisions.title: Evidence and promotion
decisions.question: Which evidence is sufficient for each claim, and which implementation changes invalidate it?
decisions.required_output: Exact source/build/host/QEMU/physical/visual/security/a11y/performance rules, receipt schema and affected-check selection.
decisions.acceptance: A stale artifact, missing required negative case, hardware skip or unsupported target cannot satisfy completion.

decisions.title: Boot generations and platform profiles
decisions.question: What are the supported media, firmware, architecture and recovery combinations?
decisions.required_output: A full matrix retaining every canonical target, bounded handover schema, selected initial rehearsal profile and explicit later qualification tasks.
decisions.acceptance: Malformed/unknown-required input rejects; each selected/previous/recovery generation is identifiable; no profile selection silently shrinks the whole programme.

decisions.title: Process construction and orphan custody
decisions.question: How are a child image, full-width identity, scheduler admission and parent ownership published atomically?
decisions.required_output: The detailed next-process contract, syscall layouts/errors, orphan transition table and allocation/admission/copyout failure matrix.
decisions.acceptance: Parent state survives every failed spawn; terminal results survive failed wait; high-bit handle generations remain valid; no child loses its owner.

decisions.title: Concurrency and CPU state
decisions.question: Which state belongs to a process, thread, CPU and interrupt frame, and how is ownership synchronized?
decisions.required_output: FP/vector/flags/TLS/stack state matrix, scheduler policy, atomics/lock ordering, TLB acknowledgement and CPU offline contracts.
decisions.acceptance: Nested interrupts, preemption, migration, faults and offline paths preserve ownership or fail-stop with a bounded diagnostic.

decisions.title: Memory and lifetime
decisions.question: How do allocation, shared mappings, COW, file cache, quotas and revocation interact?
decisions.required_output: Typed ownership and reference rules, complete accounting classes, pressure order, failure-atomic mapping/cleanup and ABI semantics.
decisions.acceptance: Every allocation/transfer/revoke failure has a deterministic expected pre/post-state and a leak oracle.

decisions.title: Authority, identity and consent
decisions.question: What rights, credentials and explicit consent does each operation require?
decisions.required_output: Handle/type/right matrix, derivation/revoke limits, credential transition matrix and operation-bound approval records.
decisions.acceptance: Source and destination rights are independent; failed credential drop prevents launch; a stale or foreign token never grants authority.

decisions.title: IPC and service lifecycle
decisions.question: How are request versions, bytes, handles, budgets, deadlines, cancellation and peer death represented?
decisions.required_output: Versioned IDL, descriptor/readiness dependencies, request state machines, crash budgets and rollback/teardown order.
decisions.acceptance: Unknown-required data, late replies, full queues and service loss have bounded typed outcomes and leave no leaked grants.

decisions.title: Cryptography, keys and trust
decisions.question: Which reviewed algorithms/libraries, keys and trust policies serve TLS, accounts, packages, storage and releases?
decisions.required_output: Version-locked primary specifications, library/license review, key custody/rotation/recovery, time policy and rejection vectors; no ad hoc cryptographic construction.
decisions.acceptance: Separate integrity from publisher authentication; prove chain/name/usage/critical-extension policy; signing and deployment still require their own authorization.

decisions.title: Device and DMA isolation
decisions.question: Which hardware can actually enforce isolation, and what happens where it cannot?
decisions.required_output: Provider resource/lifecycle contracts, IOMMU and no-IOMMU profiles, firmware custody and removal/reset state machines.
decisions.acceptance: No DMA-isolation claim on a non-isolated profile; every BAR/IRQ/DMA/endpoint reservation has a tested release path.

decisions.title: Storage durability and migration
decisions.question: What does committed mean for each block provider, filesystem and package transaction?
decisions.required_output: Flush/barrier model, on-disk versions, migration/repair/recovery policy, encrypted-volume ownership and old/new commit points.
decisions.acceptance: Power loss, reordered/torn writes, disk full and media removal preserve a defined recoverable state.

decisions.title: Display safety and presentation
decisions.question: Which owner controls scanout, surfaces, fences, cache types, panel power and fallback?
decisions.required_output: Display/surface protocol and renderer oracle, frame/input budgets, Intel power/timing/recovery sheet and approved physical procedure.
decisions.acceptance: A failed provider cannot remove the last usable display; physical timing rules come from pinned primary specifications and measured hardware.

decisions.title: Design, text and accessibility
decisions.question: Which current design rules and semantic interfaces must all apps share?
decisions.required_output: Selected PRESSWORK tokens/states, shaping/font/license policy, accessibility tree/actions, focus, IME/bidi/localization and reduced-motion/high-contrast behavior.
decisions.acceptance: Keyboard and assistive workflows operate the real effects; screenshots alone do not satisfy accessibility.

decisions.title: Network and wireless profiles
decisions.question: Which physical providers, firmware, protocol versions and remote-exposure rules are required?
decisions.required_output: Per-device/provider matrix, DNS/TLS/socket policy, fault simulator and Wi-Fi/Bluetooth association/authentication/recovery contracts.
decisions.acceptance: Virtual networking does not promote physical radios; unsupported hardware and unavailable firmware stay explicit.

decisions.title: Audio, camera and media
decisions.question: What are the stream, codec, format, timing, privacy and licensing contracts?
decisions.required_output: Negotiation/ring/clock schemas, capture grant lifetime, codec worker limits, formats, latency budgets and licensing decisions.
decisions.acceptance: Revocation stops capture; malformed content cannot own device memory; hotplug and drift have tested recovery.

decisions.title: Application and package ABI
decisions.question: What can a native app depend on across launch, update, crash, restore and removal?
decisions.required_output: Versioned ABI/SDK, manifest admission, portal contracts, document state and package compatibility/migration policy.
decisions.acceptance: A real app completes its durable workflow outside the kernel and survives denied grants and service restart.

decisions.title: Web platform and browser containment
decisions.question: Which web capabilities are implemented internally, which approved dependencies are used, and what is unsupported?
decisions.required_output: Per-capability standards/version/corpus map, process authority split, origin/storage/download/certificate policy and resource budgets.
decisions.acceptance: Every advertised web behavior has a deterministic oracle and restricted-worker failure proof; dependency choices retain licenses and provenance.

decisions.title: Application formats and workflow depth
decisions.question: What does complete mean for each office, creative, media, communication and personal app?
decisions.required_output: Every target gets explicit create/import/edit/action/save/reopen/export, offline/conflict, recovery, accessibility and performance scenarios.
decisions.acceptance: No target closes on a painted screen or a menu entry; verify durable/external effects with independent inspection.

decisions.title: Compatibility and external workloads
decisions.question: Which exact Linux, Windows, POSIX and VM workloads define the compatibility contracts?
decisions.required_output: Pinned programme/version/architecture/API matrices, port/build/dependency recipes and explicit unsupported results; all canonical compatibility features remain queued.
decisions.acceptance: Successful compilation or one demo does not imply blanket compatibility; test the full selected workflows and containment.

decisions.title: Language semantics and active engine ownership
decisions.question: Which language choices are locked, which remain design decisions, and which backend is responsible for each target?
decisions.required_output: A live-source comparison with retained language plans, explicit types/ownership/errors/ABI rules, active/archived backend map and feature parity matrix.
decisions.acceptance: Do not reopen syntax without a reason or revive archived implementations; all active engines agree on the declared semantics.

decisions.title: Bootstrap and self-hosting trust
decisions.question: How does the trusted host seed lead to a matching system rebuilt inside zlOS?
decisions.required_output: Seed, stage, compiler, linker, sysroot, source/package graph and artifact identities plus semantic and byte-level comparison rules.
decisions.acceptance: A stored hash alone is insufficient; execute the rebuilt compiler and boot the resulting exact system.

decisions.title: Agent authority and model-independent execution
decisions.question: How can agents plan and automate without becoming a new privileged authority?
decisions.required_output: Typed deterministic broker, attenuated child grants, model/tool boundaries, secret handling, approval binding, budgets and independent completion oracle.
decisions.acceptance: Hostile tool output, parent death, revoke-before-spawn and forged success cannot bypass authority or conceal unfinished effects.

decisions.title: Release, demo and support operations
decisions.question: Who may publish, sign, deploy, repair, retain support data and operate remote demos?
decisions.required_output: Exact-artifact release/runbook, lease/transport/egress model, recovery rehearsal, consent/redaction and incident/revocation procedure.
decisions.acceptance: No orphan resources, unsigned promotion, unapproved external exposure or destructive target ambiguity; publish only after explicit approval.

decisions.title: Full programme scope and unavailable hardware
decisions.question: How are later devices, architectures and historical full-stack ambitions retained without claiming unavailable proof?
decisions.required_output: A target-by-target hardware/specification/fixture/acquisition plan and explicit mapping or scope-decision record for every legacy ambition.
decisions.acceptance: No missing target is erased by choosing an initial profile; distinguish full programme completion from one qualified release.

phases.title: Preserve the baseline and make every claim traceable
phases.bounded_export: One selected source tree, working build/test oracles, declared inputs, and separate host/QEMU/physical status.

phases.title: Prove and preserve the current desktop and hardware baseline
phases.bounded_export: An exact-image regression baseline plus explicit unresolved physical claims; safe host work can proceed.

phases.title: Own the complete boot, firmware and recovery path
phases.bounded_export: Validated boot origin and typed handover with a bootable fallback; later services consume this bounded contract.

phases.title: Make independent programs a reliable kernel facility
phases.bounded_export: Bounded isolated execution, safe copy, ownership, timer scheduling and termination custody; credentials and advanced mappings join later.

phases.title: Give programs explicit authority and safe communication
phases.bounded_export: Generation-checked rights, bounded IPC and a minimal restartable supervisor with declared service identity.

phases.title: Make every device follow one lifecycle and resource contract
phases.bounded_export: Discovery, resource admission, lifecycle and common provider interfaces with honest DMA-isolation capabilities.

phases.title: Make storage, files and updates survive failure
phases.bounded_export: Bounded block/VFS/file ownership and durable transactions for process and service consumers.

phases.title: Make the desktop an owned, recoverable service
phases.bounded_export: Owned surfaces, input/focus and a bounded compositor protocol with a working software fallback.

phases.title: Make networking reliable and explicitly authorized
phases.bounded_export: Socket/resolver/network policy and a tested virtual provider; physical provider claims remain separate.

phases.title: Build audio, capture and synchronized media streams
phases.bounded_export: Audio/capture ownership, bounded rings and permission-aware streams usable by accessibility and media clients.

phases.title: Finish the shared visual, accessibility and language system
phases.bounded_export: Usable semantic primitives, themes, text and input contracts consumed by the app SDK.

phases.title: Give applications a complete runtime and shared services
phases.bounded_export: A stable app ABI/SDK, launch lifecycle and minimal file/settings/notification portals for the first isolated app.

phases.title: Migrate every existing app and game without losing behavior
phases.bounded_export: At least one fully migrated app journey; the phase stays open until all current entries and games are accounted for.

phases.title: Turn the browser into an isolated and capable web platform
phases.bounded_export: Browser UI and restricted content/network/decoder workers running a declared real corpus.

phases.title: Deliver the full application families as real workflows
phases.bounded_export: One complete application workflow per family foundation; every named destination retains its own completion gate.

phases.title: Make development tools and compatibility usable
phases.bounded_export: A PTY/process shell and reproducible tool execution suitable for bringing the zl toolchain onto zlOS.

phases.title: Complete the zl systems language and toolchain
phases.owner_scope: src/frontend/; src/runtime/; src/backends/; src/selfhost/; stdlib/; editors/
phases.bounded_export: Host-tested ABI/data/code-generation primitives and object emission for downstream work. Running the compiler inside zlOS belongs to M-16.09 and is not supplied by this early handoff.

phases.title: Add agents and automation through ordinary system authority
phases.bounded_export: A typed broker executing bounded, inspectable plans through capabilities, with cancellation and audit.

phases.title: Make releases, recovery and operations trustworthy
phases.bounded_export: An exact-artifact release/recovery rehearsal and an isolated operational control plane; publication is a separate authorized action.

phases.title: Deliver every broader hardware and architecture target
phases.bounded_export: Per-profile architecture/device contracts with independent simulation and exact physical qualification records.

phases.title: Rebuild and qualify the complete system from inside zlOS
phases.bounded_export: A matching bootable system rebuilt inside zlOS; full programme completion additionally requires every retained feature/target acceptance gate.

packages.title: driver lifecycle supervisor
packages.requirement: driver lifecycle supervisor
packages.original_contract:
**Depends on:** DA-04 through DA-06 plus process/service supervision.

**Deliver:** `Matched -> Admitted -> ResourcesReserved -> Starting -> Online ->
Degraded -> Quiescing -> Offline -> Removed`, with `Failed/Recovering/Quarantined`
branches. `Degraded` records lost functionality, user-visible effect, retry policy
and transition back to Online, Failed or Offline. Every pre-commit state can enter
`Aborting`; `abort(plan)` releases every dependency, BAR/port, IRQ, DMA map/domain,
firmware object, allocation and handle and returns a release receipt before the
device becomes Matched or Absent again.

**Invariants:** provider publication is atomic; every wait has a deadline; stop is
idempotent; remove masks interrupts and stops DMA before freeing resources; retry
budgets are finite; stale completions cannot mutate a new generation.

Every provider request carries provider epoch, device generation, request ID,
deadline, buffer provenance and cancellation state, and completes exactly once as:

```text
OK(result) | UNSUPPORTED(detail) | INVALID_INPUT(detail)
PERMISSION_DENIED(required_capability)
RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED(retryable, minimum_required) | TIMEOUT(stage)
CANCELLED(by) | DEVICE_GONE(generation) | PROVIDER_DIED(epoch)
PARTIAL(progress, continuation) | INTERNAL_ERROR(receipt_id)
```

Provider death stops admission, revokes DMA/IRQ/MMIO, settles every outstanding
request exactly once, resets or quarantines the device, and only then permits a
new provider epoch.

**Proof:** inject failure at every transition and allocation; repeated start/stop;
peer/service death; IRQ storm; timeout; reset failure; unplug with work in flight;
late IRQ/completion after resource reuse; abort after each reservation and compare
the complete resource/handle graph with pre-state.

partial-provider failure, device missing after wake, clock discontinuity, stale

cycles under I/O and app load.

**Depends on:** safe ordinary app model, DA-18/19/23/24/26.

**Deliver:** isolated model/orchestrator process, small deterministic tool broker,
compiled typed plans, consent, provenance, bounded jobs, attenuated child handles,
deadlines/revocation and independent result receipts.

**Invariants:** no ring-0 orchestrator; child grants derive at commit from live parent
handles; revoke serializes with spawn; killing parent/root makes descendants dead
and every handle stale; plugins/tools cannot gain undeclared authority.

**Proof:** revoke-then-spawn, concurrent spawn/revoke, parent/root kill, orphan
search, prompt/tool injection, deadline, queue/memory exhaustion, bad tool package,
partial effect, consent denial and independent reviewer contradiction.

tasks.title: Baseline and scope
tasks.action:
Which exact committed input and pending work belong to the next implementation generation?
Required output: A source/worktree custody ledger and explicit disposition of all 906 features, 611 targets, 174 contracts, 63 named implementations and the catalogue surface; Later/Profile labels retain scope.
tasks.acceptance: No missing or duplicate IDs; no dirty work overwritten; no historical done claim adopted without matching evidence.
tasks.owner_scope: Named subsystem owner plus affected producer/consumer owners; user decisions only where product policy or authorization is actually required.

tasks.title: Dependency and handoff semantics
tasks.action:
Which bounded interfaces can be consumed before the owning phase is fully complete?
Required output: A named producer/consumer/ABI/error/ownership/proof contract per handoff, plus the distinction between development readiness and final phase promotion.
tasks.acceptance: Resolve process/credentials, file-backed memory/VFS, host-language/target-toolchain and browser/app-platform bootstrap cycles explicitly; all executable edges must be acyclic.
tasks.owner_scope: Named subsystem owner plus affected producer/consumer owners; user decisions only where product policy or authorization is actually required.

tasks.title: Evidence and promotion
tasks.action:
Which evidence is sufficient for each claim, and which implementation changes invalidate it?
Required output: Exact source/build/host/QEMU/physical/visual/security/a11y/performance rules, receipt schema and affected-check selection.
tasks.acceptance: A stale artifact, missing required negative case, hardware skip or unsupported target cannot satisfy completion.
tasks.owner_scope: Named subsystem owner plus affected producer/consumer owners; user decisions only where product policy or authorization is actually required.

tasks.title: Boot generations and platform profiles
tasks.action:
What are the supported media, firmware, architecture and recovery combinations?
Required output: A full matrix retaining every canonical target, bounded handover schema, selected initial rehearsal profile and explicit later qualification tasks.
tasks.acceptance: Malformed/unknown-required input rejects; each selected/previous/recovery generation is identifiable; no profile selection silently shrinks the whole programme.
tasks.owner_scope: Named subsystem owner plus affected producer/consumer owners; user decisions only where product policy or authorization is actually required.

tasks.title: Process construction and orphan custody
tasks.action:
How are a child image, full-width identity, scheduler admission and parent ownership published atomically?
Required output: The detailed next-process contract, syscall layouts/errors, orphan transition table and allocation/admission/copyout failure matrix.
tasks.acceptance: Parent state survives every failed spawn; terminal results survive failed wait; high-bit handle generations remain valid; no child loses its owner.
tasks.owner_scope: Named subsystem owner plus affected producer/consumer owners; user decisions only where product policy or authorization is actually required.

tasks.title: Concurrency and CPU state
tasks.action:
Which state belongs to a process, thread, CPU and interrupt frame, and how is ownership synchronized?
Required output: FP/vector/flags/TLS/stack state matrix, scheduler policy, atomics/lock ordering, TLB acknowledgement and CPU offline contracts.
tasks.acceptance: Nested interrupts, preemption, migration, faults and offline paths preserve ownership or fail-stop with a bounded diagnostic.
tasks.owner_scope: Named subsystem owner plus affected producer/consumer owners; user decisions only where product policy or authorization is actually required.

tasks.title: Memory and lifetime
tasks.action:
How do allocation, shared mappings, COW, file cache, quotas and revocation interact?
Required output: Typed ownership and reference rules, complete accounting classes, pressure order, failure-atomic mapping/cleanup and ABI semantics.
tasks.acceptance: Every allocation/transfer/revoke failure has a deterministic expected pre/post-state and a leak oracle.
tasks.owner_scope: Named subsystem owner plus affected producer/consumer owners; user decisions only where product policy or authorization is actually required.

tasks.title: Authority, identity and consent
tasks.action:
What rights, credentials and explicit consent does each operation require?
Required output: Handle/type/right matrix, derivation/revoke limits, credential transition matrix and operation-bound approval records.
tasks.acceptance: Source and destination rights are independent; failed credential drop prevents launch; a stale or foreign token never grants authority.
tasks.owner_scope: Named subsystem owner plus affected producer/consumer owners; user decisions only where product policy or authorization is actually required.

tasks.title: IPC and service lifecycle
tasks.action:
How are request versions, bytes, handles, budgets, deadlines, cancellation and peer death represented?
Required output: Versioned IDL, descriptor/readiness dependencies, request state machines, crash budgets and rollback/teardown order.
tasks.acceptance: Unknown-required data, late replies, full queues and service loss have bounded typed outcomes and leave no leaked grants.
tasks.owner_scope: Named subsystem owner plus affected producer/consumer owners; user decisions only where product policy or authorization is actually required.

tasks.title: Deliver — driver lifecycle supervisor
tasks.action:
`Matched -> Admitted -> ResourcesReserved -> Starting -> Online ->
Degraded -> Quiescing -> Offline -> Removed`, with `Failed/Recovering/Quarantined`
branches. `Degraded` records lost functionality, user-visible effect, retry policy
and transition back to Online, Failed or Offline. Every pre-commit state can enter
`Aborting`; `abort(plan)` releases every dependency, BAR/port, IRQ, DMA map/domain,
firmware object, allocation and handle and returns a release receipt before the
device becomes Matched or Absent again.
tasks.acceptance: Satisfy every obligation in the preserved Deliver field for DA-07.
constraints: Do not start implementation until the package dependency/contract review is accepted.
Use existing implementations and contracts; these work packages are not instructions to build duplicates.

tasks.title: Invariants — driver lifecycle supervisor
tasks.action:
provider publication is atomic; every wait has a deadline; stop is
idempotent; remove masks interrupts and stops DMA before freeing resources; retry
budgets are finite; stale completions cannot mutate a new generation.

Every provider request carries provider epoch, device generation, request ID,
deadline, buffer provenance and cancellation state, and completes exactly once as:

```text
OK(result) | UNSUPPORTED(detail) | INVALID_INPUT(detail)
PERMISSION_DENIED(required_capability)
RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED(retryable, minimum_required) | TIMEOUT(stage)
CANCELLED(by) | DEVICE_GONE(generation) | PROVIDER_DIED(epoch)
PARTIAL(progress, continuation) | INTERNAL_ERROR(receipt_id)
```

Provider death stops admission, revokes DMA/IRQ/MMIO, settles every outstanding
request exactly once, resets or quarantines the device, and only then permits a
new provider epoch.
